recipes.name: Beef Tenderloin With Roasted Shallots
ingredients_raw: 0.75 pound shallots, halved lengthwise and peeled

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). In 9 inch pie pan, toss shallots with oil to coat. Season with salt and pepper. Roast until shallots are deep brown and very tender, stirring occasionally, about 30 minutes.
In a large saucepan, combine beef broth and port. Bring to a boil. Cook over high heat until the volume is reduced by half, about 30 minutes. Whisk in tomato paste. Set aside.

Pat beef dry; sprinkle with thyme, salt and pepper. In a large roasting pan, set over medium heat on the stove top, saute bacon until golden. Using a slotted spoon, transfer bacon to paper towels. Add beef to pan; brown on all sides over medium high heat, about 7 minutes.

Transfer pan to oven. Roast beef until meat thermometer inserted into center registers 125 degrees F (50 degrees C) for medium rare, about 25 minutes. Transfer beef to platter. Tent loosely with foil.

Spoon fat off top of pan drippings in roasting pan. Place pan over high heat on stove top. Add broth mixture, and bring to boil; stir to scrape up any browned bits. Transfer to a medium saucepan, and bring to simmer. Mix 1 1/2 tablespoon butter and flour in small bowl to form smooth paste; whisk into broth mixture, and simmer until sauce thickens. Whisk in remaining butter. Stir in roasted shallots and reserved bacon. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut beef into 1/2 inch thick slices. Spoon some sauce over, and garnish with watercress.

raw_recipe.headline: Beef Tenderloin With Roasted Shallots
raw_recipe.description: This tenderloin roast makes a good company dinner. It is similar to Beef Bourguignon, but requires considerably less cooking time. Roasted shallots are added to the sauce along with sauteed bacon bits. The recipe serves 6 and can be doubled.

review.reviewBody: Believe all these raving reviews. It really is that good! I made this for a dinner party of 15 people last night with a 5 1/2 lb. tenderloin. I was worried about timing the preparation of the meat along with the other sidedishes, so I prepared some of this ahead of time. I roasted the shallots & boiled the wine/broth combination the day before and stored these in the refrigerator. Then I cooked the bacon a couple of hours ahead of time, set it aside to cool and allowed the pan it cooked in to sit on the stovetop. I took the suggestion of a couple of other posters and put the wine/broth mix, the bacon & shallots into the blender to make a smooth sauce. This was really wonderful! After roasting the tenderloin, I poured the smooth sauce into the same pan, whisked in the butter and flour and Voila! - an incredible tasting gravy to spoon over a moist & tender cut of meat. I did roast the tenderloin longer because many of my guests like beef more well done. Even with that, it still could be cut with a fork. My husband and I can't wait to try this again with a more medium rare piece of meat. I've tried many wonderful dishes from Allrecipes, but this one is the very best.

Delicious! I also made and puréed the bacon/shallot sauce the day before and just used red wine on hand, then reheated the bacon grease to brown the loin the next day. I didn’t create a butter/flour paste, just reheated the sauce and dumped them in then whisked it really well with some drippings and scraped up roast bits from the pan. Served with mashed potatoes, rolls and asparagus. Everyone wiped their plates with the rolls!

Made this for Christmas dinner with about a 6lb tenderloin. The sauce is excellent! I doubled it because I like a lot of sauce and made the broth/wine reduction a day early along with the roasted shallots. I followed others and fried the bacon in a cast iron pan, then seared the beef in it. When I was ready to make the gravy, I skimmed some of the fat out, melted butter and added the flour to make a roux. Then I added the broth/wine reduction. I blended some of the shallots and bacon with a bit of the broth in a food processor to make it thicker and because I didn’t want chunks of shallots in the gravy. I pulled the beef out of the fridge and let it sit at room temperature for a couple hours before patting it dry and seasoning it. It only took a hour (if that) to cook. I had a temperature probe in and cooked it to medium (about 140 degrees).

I made this roast in the crockpot, but tried to keep the privy recipe as intact as possible. I browned the roast in the bacon grease, but waited to add the bacon (& toasted shallots) just before serving. I didn’t cook down the sauce, to make sure there was enough to cover the meat in the crockpot. I made a couple of substitutions based on what I had available, such as red cooking wine for port, and chicken broth for beef broth. I think I will use beef broth the next time, to ensure better flavor. (I think I would not have had to add extra salt/pepper if I had used the correct broth.) I also added some chopped onions to the bottom of the crockpot to give the meat good flavor while it cooked. I added cut up potatoes and carrots to cook with the meat in the crockpot. Even with all these changes, it came out really well!

This was excellent! I made bacon the day before for breakfast, so I just put aside a few slices and chopped them, and saved some bacon drippings. I heated the drippings in a heavy pan, seared the roast, removed the excess drippings and put the pan in the oven to finish cooking. I started the gravy earlier by roasting the shallots and cooking down the port/broth. I didn't make a paste with the flour and butter, I made one roux with flour and butter and one with rice flour and butter, and split the broth/port/pan juices between the two. They both came out great, so the rice flour is a very good option for g/f folks! (Just watch the broth ingredients!!) We paired it with Chef John's Fondant Potato recipe and some roasted asparagus with parmesan. It was an impressive meal!

This was amazing! Top notch. The most tender piece of meat, and with the shallot sauce... flavor dynamite. I made a 7lb beef tenderloin for Christmas dinner. Followed the cooking instructions. I personally like my meat rare so next time I'll take it out at 120°. Temp climbed to 135° while resting and came out to a perfect medium rare. The day before I made the sauce minus the drippings and the butter-flour mixture (added while meat rested). I also roasted garlic along with the shallots and pureed in a blender. I served with roasted Brussel sprouts and twice baked potatoes. Guests were dropping forks and moaning this was so good. Delicious!

Used the reduced sodium beef broth,blended the shallots and bacon and broth mixture in the cusinart ahead of time. Was a lot of preparation, but was so good. Cooked mushrooms separate for josh, justin and myself and added on top of tenderloin. Made Christmas 2015, The boys gobbled it up and said the best Christmas dinner so far!!

I absolutely loved this! The recipe was awesome. I did make some changes based off of many other reviews by using a regular red wine instead of the port. I used a cab. I also blended the broth wine mixture when it was finished with the roasted shallots and bacon. Omg it was heaven. I wanted this instead of a special occasion dinner, just a nice dinner with the hubby, so I got two nice filets. the bake time is shorter but used the same amount of sauce for our mashed potatoes. I'm not going to cook filet any other way now. I served it with Parmesan baked asparagus and the mashed potato recipe from epicurious. Who knew that a potato ricer made such fluffy potatoes? One of the best dinners I've made. Next time, I'll probably make the sauce the night before just to make it easier though

The very first time I have left a note to give feedback on a recipe. My husband loved it! I served it with the roasted vegetables recipe also from this site and the only thing I did differently is to use potatoes tomatoes carrots and onions for the vegetables along with a tablespoon of Worchestershire sauce. Otherwise I was faithful to both recipes although I did put the sauce for the steaks through the blender like other readers suggested and it turned out beautifully! I made 4 large tenderloins so we are going to be able to eat this for three nights! Thank you very much! This will be what we serve when we have company!

Made this for Christmas Eve dinner. I couldn’t splurge for the tenderloin, so I followed all the instructions but with a round top steak (I browned the meat), and then I put everything in the crockpot for a few hours. I pulled the meat out before serving it, and blended everything else for a smooth gravy. Served over mashed potatoes with a side of Brussels Sprouts- it was delicious, and the whole family loved it. Fantastic recipe- this one is definitely a keeper!

I followed the advise of another reviewer who made the gravy the day before and put the roasted shallots, bacon and the the wine sauce in the blender. (I used red wine instead of port)
 I also rubbed the beef with the salt, pepper and thyme and browned the beef in the bacon drippings the night before and placed it back in the fridge. The beef tenderloin was so moist you could cut in with a butter knife. The gravy was amazing! I can't wait to make it again!

I'm a 74 year-old man who has made this recipe four times for family gatherings. Every time I make it I grumble about the recipes' complexity but my family appreciates it so much that it I continue to make it.

Have made this recipe exactly as written, and also as others by blending the shallots into the sauce, ahead of time. Blending does save time, but the recipe is so much better tasting in my opinion as written. Blending made a much sweeter tasting sauce. PERFECT AS WRITTEN.
Was a restaurant quality dish. Everyone loved it.
The BEST Beef Tenderloin Recipe I have ever served/eaten!! A must for any special occasion!

Followed suggestions and pureed the sauce, we doubled the gravy too for a 5lb roast. I recommend cooking the shallots in a skillet (much easier). Tasted great! Cook time was way off! It took about 1 hour to get to medium/medium rare for a 5lb roast. Fyi 125=raw. I recommend cooking it at 425 for about 50 minutes.
This was delicious. Stunning. Some of the best beef I’ve ever had, let alone made. You won’t regret making it.
4/9/23: Made this recipe so many times (looks like 13 yrs since I’m updating the review) and always a winner! 12/2010:Made this for Christmas dinner and it was loved by all! Awesome recipe!

This is an elegant main dish that I have made many times for special company meals. The shallot sauce is scrumptious and the cooking method for the tenderloin makes it an easy dish for entertaining. I do the browning and sauce prep earlier in the afternoon, then pop the meat in the over 1/2 hour before I want to serve dinner. Great to not get stuck in the kitchen with guests in the living room! It is terrific with Yukon gold potatoes smashed with butter and sour cream.
